ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-01.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-01.body:
The hands are at $90^\circ$ twice in almost every hour, because the minute hand gains $360^\circ-30^\circ=330^\circ$ per hour on the hour hand. In 12 hours the minute hand gains $11$ full turns, and the angle between the hands passes $90^\circ$ (once as it opens to $90^\circ$ and once as it closes from $270^\circ$) twice per gained turn: $2\times 11=22$. The clock shows 2:00, where the angle is $60^\circ$, so no instant is double counted at the start or end.

**Answer: 22**

ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-02.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-02.body:
A kite has two equal angles (between a long and a short side) and the other two angles are the smallest angle $x$ and its opposite angle $4x$. The angles add to $360^\circ$.

(a) $115+115+x+4x=360$, so $5x=130$ and $x=26$.

(b) $5x+5x+x+4x=360$, so $15x=360$ and $x=24$.

**Answer: (a) $26^\circ$, (b) $24^\circ$**

ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-03.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-03.body:
(a) The numerator is $8!=40320$. The denominator is $1+2-3+4-5+6+7+8=20$. So the value is $40320/20=2016$.

(b) Each term is double the previous one, so the sum is $2^{11}-2^5=2048-32=2016$ (or add: $32+64+128+256+512+1024=2016$).

**Answer: (a) 2016, (b) 2016**

ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-04.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-04.body:
The vowel o appears only in rhombus (7 letters) and parallelogram (13 letters), so one of them is needed; rhombus is shorter and also supplies u. We still need a, e and i. Trapezium (9 letters) contains all of a, e, i, so rhombus + trapezium works with $7+9=16$ letters. Alternatives are longer: rhombus + kite (i, e) + square (a) has $7+4+6=17$ letters, and using parallelogram costs at least 13 letters plus more for i.

**Answer: trapezium and rhombus (16 letters)**

ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-05.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-05.body:
Team $B$ scored no goals, so the $B$ v $C$ draw was 0-0, and $B$ lost to $A$ with $B$ scoring 0. So $C$ scored all 3 goals against $A$, and $A$ won that match, scoring at least 4 goals against $C$. Let $A$ score $k$ goals against $C$ and $11-k$ against $B$. We need $k\ge4$ and $11-k\ge1$, so $k=4,5,\dots,10$: 7 possibilities.

**Answer: 7**

ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-06.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-06.body:
Let each share be $s$. What remains: $3\times\frac s2+\frac{2s}3+\frac{3s}4=\frac{18s+8s+9s}{12}=\frac{35s}{12}$. Then $\frac{35s}{12}=700$, so $s=700\times\frac{12}{35}=240$.

**Answer: £240**

ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-07.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-07.body:
The sum of the first $n$ odd numbers is $n^2$. There are $500$ odd numbers from 1 to 999, so the total is $500^2=250\,000$.

Check by pairing: $1+999=1000$, $3+997=1000$, ... gives 250 pairs, $250\times1000=250\,000$.

**Answer: 250 000**

ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-08.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-08.body:
Jon is between Charlie and Sam, so the 81 m is split in the ratio $1:2$ (Jon to Charlie : Jon to Sam): Jon is 27 m behind Charlie and 54 m ahead of Sam. Charlie is $40-27=13$ m from the finish, so Sam has $13+81=94$ m to run.

**Answer: 94 metres**

ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-09.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-09.body:
Of three consecutive integers the middle one is even, so the two primes are the first and the third: twin primes $p,p+2$ with the middle number $p+1$. The twin primes between 21 and 99 are $(29,31),(41,43),(59,61),(71,73)$. The digit sums of the three numbers are: $29,30,31$: $11+3+4=18$; $41,42,43$: $5+6+7=18$; $59,60,61$: $14+6+7=27$; $71,72,73$: $8+9+10=27$. So the two sets are $59,60,61$ and $71,72,73$.

**Answer: 71, 72, 73 and 59, 60, 61**

ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-10.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-regional-group-10.body:
Let the integer be $N$. Placing 1 after it gives $10N+1$; placing 1 before it gives $100000+N$. So $10N+1=3(100000+N)$, i.e. $7N=299999$ and $N=42857$.

Check: $428571=3\times142857$.

**Answer: 42857**
